headline: SeedBank Launches, Bringing Professional Lawn Care to the Local Community
author: Jordan McAllister
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — A new lawn care and landscaping company, SeedBank, officially opened for business this week, offering mowing, trimming, edging, cleanup, and general yard care to residential and commercial customers across the area.

The company is led by General Manager Cesar, who oversees daily operations, coordinates the team, and schedules jobs to keep customers happy. He's joined by Weston, who manages the books and helps set pricing as Finance & Accounting Manager; Tshawn, who runs marketing and outreach as Marketing & Sales Coordinator; and Colton, who keeps equipment and field crews running smoothly as Operations Manager.
"Our goal is simple — reliable, quality lawn care delivered with a smile," the founding team said in a statement announcing the launch. SeedBank is now hiring Field Agents to help meet early demand.
Shares of SeedBank (SEED) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Bleu Room Opens Its Doors, Serving Up Multi-Cuisine Favorites in a Stylish New Space
author: Priya Chandrasekar
body: "Our goal is fast, smooth service without losing the personal touch," says General Manager Marcus Spinks, describing the vision behind Bleu Room, the new restaurant that opened this week blending comforting classics with bold international flavors in a stylish, welcoming space.

Spinks oversees both the front-of-house and kitchen at the new Clarksville spot. He's supported by Marketing Coordinator Yucheng Weng, who handles digital and print campaigns; Financial Manager Jack Hicks, who keeps the books balanced and pricing sharp; and Floor Manager Ace Doane, who keeps the dining room running and guests smiling.
The restaurant is now hiring for its kitchen, with an open Cook/Dishwasher position for anyone passionate about food preparation.
Shares of Bleu Room (BLEU) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Bubbles & Barks Brings Mobile Dog Grooming Straight to Local Driveways
author: Sam O'Rourke
body: Local dog owners no longer have to make the trip to a grooming salon. A new mobile dog wash and grooming business, Bubbles & Barks, launched this week with a fleet of equipped grooming vans ready to bring baths, brushing, trims, and nail care right to customers' homes.

At the helm is Manager Kristen Abrams, who oversees daily operations, schedules appointments, and keeps quality high across the growing team. She's joined by Sales Manager Addy Hofmans, who books appointments and grows the customer base; Marketing Coordinator Riley Denote, who spreads the word through social media and local promotions; and IT Support lead Harmony James, who keeps the booking system and payment technology running smoothly.

The company says it's aiming to become a dependable local service that keeps dogs clean and comfortable while making life easier for their owners, and is now hiring its tenth groomer as it completes staffing for five mobile vans.
Shares of Bubbles & Barks (BARK) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Pease Beez Debuts All-Natural, Honey-Based Health and Beauty Line
author: Elena Vasquez
body: Natural, simple, humane, healthy — those four words guide everything at Pease Beez, a new health and beauty company built around hand-made honey-based products that launched this week with a mission to bring natural, whole-body wellness to customers looking for simpler, more humane alternatives to typical beauty products.

General Manager Emme Dressler leads the company as primary manager, overseeing daily operations and key business decisions. She's joined by Sales Manager Tori Ross, who manages customer relationships and sales channels; Marketing Coordinator Ameila Pease, who builds brand awareness through advertising and social media; and Product Manager Major Peevyhouse, who oversees the quality and development of the company's honey-based goods.

"We're a new business with big hopes of becoming one of the world's largest health and beauty companies," the team said. Pease Beez is now hiring an IT Support specialist to help build out its online presence.
Shares of Pease Beez (BEEZ) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Stone Age Climbing & Fitness Opens Doors to Clarksville's Newest Rock Climbing Gym
author: Marcus Whitfield
body: Shares of Stone Age Climbing & Fitness (CRAG) opened trading at $15.00 today as the company celebrated the launch of one of the area's only dedicated rock climbing gyms, paired with a full strength-training and fitness facility for members of all skill levels.

General Manager Robert Simons oversees the gym as primary manager, ensuring operations run smoothly, safely, and effectively. He's joined by Marketing Manager Bailey Battles, who works to attract and retain members; Storekeeper Kale Patterson, who runs the retail side and equipment sales; and Financial Advisor Traden Lundrigan, who manages the company's budget and funding.

"We want to build a community that cares for and challenges each other — and become Stronger by Nature," the team said. The gym is now hiring a Trainer to help lead group sessions for beginners through advanced climbers.

headline: My Pick for Clarksville's Best New Business Concept of 2026: Stone Age Climbing & Fitness
author: Jordyn Everhart, Local Fitness Influencer
body: I try a lot of new fitness spots around Clarksville for my page, and it's rare that one earns a spontaneous shoutout instead of a scheduled review. Stone Age Climbing & Fitness just earned my vote for 2026's Best New Business Concept in town — and I don't hand that out lightly.

Here's the pitch, in case you haven't heard: it's one of the only dedicated rock climbing gyms in the area, paired with a full strength-training and fitness facility, so you're not choosing between a climbing session and a regular gym day. It's all under one roof.

As a creator, what stood out to me is how much this place gives me to work with. The gym's new Trainer role is built around changing the climbing routes every single month, which means there's always something new on the wall to film, attempt, and occasionally fail at on camera. And because the space is set up for total beginners and serious climbers alike, a first-timer post and an advanced-technique post can both live on the same feed without feeling out of place — that's harder to pull off than it sounds.

General Manager Robert Simons and the team have been clear that the goal isn't just memberships — it's building "a community that cares for and challenges each other," and you can feel that intention in how the gym is staffing up. They're currently hiring a Trainer who has to be belay and climbing rescue certified, which tells me safety isn't an afterthought here — it's part of the culture from day one, and that's exactly what I want to be able to tell my followers before I send them somewhere new.

Add in a dedicated retail and equipment setup run by Storekeeper Kale Patterson and the financial groundwork Financial Advisor Traden Lundrigan and Marketing Manager Bailey Battles are laying to grow the brand, and it's easy to see why this is my pick for the year. The market seems to agree: shares of Stone Age Climbing & Fitness (CRAG) climbed $2.00 today, closing at $17.00, on the news.

headline: Crosshairs & Scriptures Launches Faith-Inspired Outdoor Apparel Line
author: Nadia Okafor
body: Graphic t-shirts, hats, and accessories designed for customers who want to show their faith alongside their love of hunting and the outdoors hit the market this week as Crosshairs & Scriptures, a new Christian outdoor-inspired apparel brand, officially launched.

General Manager Joel Gish leads the business as primary manager, overseeing final decisions and keeping the team organized around its product roadmap. He's joined by Marketing Manager Richard, who runs the brand's social media presence; Sales Manager Kingston, who manages customer orders and looks for ways to grow sales; and Product Manager Brennon, who develops new designs and oversees inventory.
The company sells its apparel through an online store and social media, with a mission to create products that let customers represent both their faith and their outdoor lifestyle.
Shares of Crosshairs & Scriptures (AMEN) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Coffee Trip Rolls Out a Moving Cafe, Bringing Coffee and Baked Goods Anywhere
author: Derek Lindqvist
body: Rent the cafe. Get the coffee. That's the pitch behind Coffee Trip, a new mobile cafe business that launched this week promising a fresh cup of coffee and baked goods served with a smile, anywhere, at any time.

General Manager Annika Sosa leads the company as primary manager, planning and organizing operations to keep things running smoothly. She's joined by Financial Manager Timmy, who advises on the company's financial health and strategy, and Marketing Coordinator Kamiyah Hollins, who makes sure campaigns reach the right audience.
The small team says it's focused on doing a few things well: friendly service, quality coffee, and flexibility to show up wherever customers need them.
Shares of Coffee Trip (JAVA) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Frontier Kitchen Opens for Business, Serving Up a New Dining Experience
author: Callie Ashworth
body: Frontier Kitchen opened its doors this week, bringing a new restaurant to the local hospitality scene with a focus on strong daily operations and a memorable menu and brand experience for guests.

General Manager Maddy Kosturko leads the restaurant as primary manager, assigning tasks, coordinating staff schedules, and keeping the team aligned with customer service standards. She's joined by Sales Manager Freddy Monroe, who trains staff on menu recommendations and works to boost repeat visits; Marketing Manager Truman Gill, who runs social media and promotes special events; and Finance Manager Troy Campbell, who tracks the budget and keeps the business on solid financial footing.
Founded in 2024 according to its branding, Frontier Kitchen is now staffing up its front-of-house and kitchen teams as it settles into the local dining scene.
Shares of Frontier Kitchen (GRUB) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Natura Energy Launches All-Natural Energy Drink Line
author: Theo Bramwell
body: The energy drink aisle has a new all-natural contender. Natura Energy launched this week with a lineup of energy drinks aimed at giving customers a healthier alternative to typical options on the market.

The company is led by Aniyah, who serves as Overseer and primary manager, keeping operations running smoothly and the team aligned with company goals. She's joined by Jodi Miller, who leads marketing and brand awareness; Natalie, who handles HR and customer service; and Mia, who manages sales strategy and the company's finances.
Natura Energy says its mission is simple: supply healthier, all-natural energy drinks to the public. The company is now hiring an IT Specialist Manager to help support its growing technology needs.
Shares of Natura Energy (VOLT) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Chosen Academy Opens as an All-Inclusive Recreation Center for Everyone
author: Malik Renshaw
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — Chosen Academy, a new all-inclusive gym and recreation center, opened this week with a facility lineup that includes workout equipment, a pool, basketball courts, an indoor soccer field, dance studios, and tennis courts.

The center is led by General Manager Triston Hauser, who oversees the growth and success of all Chosen Academy facilities — from gym finances and daily operations to member satisfaction and facility upkeep. He's joined by Earnest Williams, who leads staff recruitment and local relations as HR Director and Event Coordinator; Lilly Evans, who runs the dance and fitness class program as Dance and Class Coordinator; and Dwjuan Bradford, who organizes athletic events and areas as Athletic Coordinator.

"We're empowering individuals to be the best version of themselves through fitness, recreation, and movement," the team said, adding that the mission extends to staff as well as members. Chosen Academy is now hiring a Social Media Marketing Manager to help grow its presence in the local community.
Shares of Chosen Academy (CHZN) opened trading at $15.00 today.

headline: Clarksville Family Blames SeedBank Lawn Treatment After Dog Falls Ill
author: Denise Okonkwo
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — A local family says their dog became sick within hours of playing on a lawn serviced earlier that day by SeedBank, and the resulting Facebook post has spread quickly through neighborhood groups this week.

The family, who posted in the "Clarksville Neighbors" Facebook group, said their Labrador, Biscuit, began vomiting and acting lethargic that evening. "He was fine that morning. A few hours after the SeedBank crew left, he wouldn't even get up for dinner," the post reads. The post tags SeedBank directly and has been shared more than 400 times, with over 200 comments as of this morning.

Several commenters described similar reactions in their own pets after recent SeedBank visits, including itchy paws and excessive drooling, though others in the thread defended the company, saying they've used SeedBank for over a year with no issues. The family's veterinarian said Biscuit's symptoms are "consistent with exposure to a lawn chemical" but said bloodwork to confirm a specific cause is still pending.
At least three commenters in the thread said they were canceling upcoming SeedBank appointments "until this gets sorted out." SeedBank General Manager Cesar has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Viral Post Alleging Health Code Violation Rattles Bleu Room, Reservations Slow
author: Priya Chandrasekar
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — A social media post claiming Bleu Room was cited for a health code violation has circulated widely since Wednesday night, and the restaurant's reservation platform shows a noticeable drop in bookings for the coming weekend.

The post, which includes a photo the poster says was taken inside Bleu Room's kitchen, claims a health inspector "wrote the restaurant up" for unsanitary conditions. It has been shared several hundred times across local community pages, with many commenters saying they'll be avoiding the restaurant until more information comes out.

A review of publicly available Clarksville-Montgomery County health inspection records by this outlet did not turn up any recent citation on file for Bleu Room, and the restaurant's most recent inspection score is not yet posted. It's unclear where the photo originated or whether it was taken at Bleu Room at all.

"I had a reservation for Saturday and canceled it as soon as I saw the post — better safe than sorry," one would-be diner told this outlet. Bleu Room General Manager Marcus Spinks has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Bubbles & Barks Customer Accuses Mobile Groomer of Negligence After Dog Comes Home Injured
author: Sam O'Rourke
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — A Bubbles & Barks customer says her goldendoodle came home from a scheduled grooming appointment with a visible nick near his ear and a patch shaved noticeably closer than the rest of his coat, and photos she posted to a local pet owners' Facebook group have drawn hundreds of comments since Thursday.

"Cooper is my baby and he came home looking like this," wrote the owner, Jenna Whitcomb, alongside close-up photos of the nick and the uneven patch. "I trusted them to come to my house and take care of him and this is what I got." The post directly tags Bubbles & Barks and has been shared widely within the group.

Reactions in the comment thread are mixed. Several other customers said they've had consistently good experiences with the company's mobile groomers, while at least one other commenter said she noticed a similar close-shaved patch on her own dog after a visit earlier this summer but hadn't said anything at the time.
Whitcomb says she has not yet been able to reach anyone at the company directly. Bubbles & Barks Manager Kristen Abrams has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Pease Beez Customers Say Signature Balm 'Isn't the Same' — and Say No One Told Them Why
author: Marcus Whitfield
body: A growing number of Pease Beez customers say the company quietly changed the formula of one of its best-selling products without any public announcement, and that the company let the change go unmentioned for weeks before customers started noticing on their own.

According to a copy of the ingredient label reviewed by this outlet, the current version of the brand's flagship lip and skin balm lists a different order and ratio of ingredients than the label pictured in the company's own product photos from earlier this summer, with no updated "new formula" messaging anywhere on the packaging or website. Two former part-time employees, who asked not to be named because they no longer work for the company, told this outlet that the recipe was adjusted internally back in July and that staff were told not to bring it up with customers unless directly asked.

"I've bought this balm for two years and I know how it's supposed to feel going on," wrote one customer, Priya Nandakumar, in a one-star review posted to the company's online store this week. "This one is thinner, barely smells like honey anymore, and doesn't work nearly as well on my hands. Nobody said a word about changing it." Her review has been echoed by more than a dozen others over the past several days, several using nearly identical language — "different," "watered down," "not what I paid for" — and a handful accusing the company of trying to cut costs without telling anyone.

The complaints have spilled onto social media as well. A side-by-side photo comparing two lip balm tins from different purchase dates, posted to a local buy-sell-trade group, has been shared dozens of times with the caption "did anyone else notice Pease Beez changed their formula and just... didn't say anything?" Several commenters said they'd noticed a difference for weeks but assumed it was their imagination until seeing the post.
It remains unclear why the change was not disclosed to customers or when, if ever, the company intended to announce it. Pease Beez General Manager Emme Dressler has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Serious Fall at Stone Age Climbing & Fitness Prompts Membership Cancellations, Insurance Concerns
author: Jordan McAllister
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — A member at Stone Age Climbing & Fitness suffered a serious fall from the climbing wall during an evening session earlier this week and was taken to the hospital, according to multiple accounts posted in the gym's member community group.

Details of the member's condition have not been made public. Several witnesses who posted about the incident online raised questions about whether route difficulty ratings and safety-gear checks were properly followed that evening, though none of the accounts have been independently verified.

"I love this gym but I'm seriously reconsidering my membership after seeing what happened," one member wrote in a post that has drawn dozens of replies, some defending the gym's safety record and others echoing the member's concerns. The incident comes just weeks after the gym was publicly recognized as 2026's Best New Business Concept in town.

Industry sources say a serious injury claim like this one could push the gym's liability insurance premiums higher regardless of fault. Stone Age Climbing & Fitness General Manager Robert Simons has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Crosshairs & Scriptures Hit With Cease-and-Desist Over Best-Selling Design
author: Nadia Okafor
body: Crosshairs & Scriptures has reportedly received a cease-and-desist letter from another outdoor apparel company alleging that its best-selling "Called Home" design — a deer-and-cross graphic featured on t-shirts and hats — infringes on a registered design the other company says it owns.

The "Called Home" design is said to account for a significant share of the brand's online sales this quarter, and the listing has already been marked "temporarily unavailable" on the company's online store as of this morning.

Customers who purchased the shirt took to social media with confused reactions, several asking whether the product is being pulled entirely and a few reposting side-by-side comparison images of the two designs in question to debate how similar they actually are.

It is not yet clear whether Crosshairs & Scriptures plans to contest the claim, redesign the product, or pull it permanently. Crosshairs & Scriptures General Manager Joel Gish has been contacted for comment.

headline: Video Showing Rodent Near Coffee Trip Cart at Farmers Market Prompts Health Department Tag
author: Derek Lindqvist
body: A shopper at Saturday's Riverside Farmers Market posted a video appearing to show a rat scurrying near the wheels of the Coffee Trip mobile cafe cart, tagging the county health department directly in the caption. The video has been viewed thousands of times since it went up.

"I was literally about to order a latte when I saw this thing run right under the cart," the poster wrote. Comments on the video are split — some expressing concern about buying food or drinks from the cart going forward, others pointing out the rodent could have come from a neighboring stall rather than the cart itself.

"I don't know if it's fair to blame Coffee Trip specifically, but I'll admit it made me hesitate before ordering," one market regular told this outlet. The health department has not confirmed whether it has opened any inquiry related to the video.
Coffee Trip General Manager Annika Sosa has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Former Frontier Kitchen Employee Alleges Shorted Tips, Mistreatment; Coworkers Weigh In Online
author: Callie Ashworth
body: A former server at Frontier Kitchen posted a lengthy statement on social media this week alleging she was regularly shorted on tips during closing shifts and describing what she called a dismissive response from management when she raised the issue before leaving the job.

The post has been shared widely and drawn dozens of comments, including several from accounts identifying themselves as current or former Frontier Kitchen staff. Some voiced support and described similar experiences with shift pay; others pushed back, saying their own experience with scheduling and pay at the restaurant had been positive.

"Reading this as someone who still works there... this isn't the whole picture, but it's also not nothing," one comment reads. The thread has continued to grow through the day, with new comments from people identifying as regular customers weighing in as well.

The allegations surface as Frontier Kitchen is actively hiring for a new Event Planner role in Nashville, part of the company's push to expand its events business. Frontier Kitchen General Manager Maddy Kosturko has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Teen Hospitalized After Drinking Multiple Natura Energy Cans, Raising Questions About Marketing
author: Carla Jimenez
body: A local teenager was hospitalized over the weekend after reportedly drinking several cans of Natura Energy in a short period at a gathering, according to a family friend who posted about the incident online. The teen is said to have experienced a rapid heartbeat and dizziness before being taken to the hospital; the family has not spoken publicly and has not been named.

The post, which has since been shared beyond the original group it was posted in, has prompted a wider conversation about who energy drinks like Natura Energy are being marketed to and how their "all natural" branding is perceived. "Since when do teenagers drink energy drinks like they're sodas?" one commenter wrote in a thread that has drawn hundreds of replies.

Natura Energy's marketing has emphasized its all-natural ingredient list since launch, but some commenters online are questioning whether that framing makes the product seem safer to drink in larger quantities than it actually is — a question this outlet has not independently verified with medical experts.
Natura Energy Overseer Aniyah has been contacted for a statement.

headline: Chosen Academy Members Report Fraudulent Charges After Possible Data Breach
author: Trevor Lin
body: Several Chosen Academy members say they've discovered unauthorized charges on the same payment cards they use for their gym memberships, and a growing thread on a local subreddit suggests the common link may be the recreation center's payment system.

One member, whose post has since been deleted but was screenshotted and re-shared by others, described canceling her card after two unfamiliar charges appeared just days after she renewed her Chosen Academy membership online. At least four other members have since replied to similar threads describing the same pattern.

"I renewed my membership, and less than a week later I've got charges from a company I've never heard of," one member wrote in a post on Chosen Academy's own community page. As of this morning, the company's social accounts have not addressed the reports, and no post acknowledging the issue has been made.
Chosen Academy General Manager Triston Hauser has been contacted for a statement.

headline: SeedBank Pledges to Pull Chemical If Link to Pet Illness Is Confirmed
author: Denise Okonkwo
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — SeedBank issued a public statement Thursday addressing the viral Facebook post in which a local family said their dog, Biscuit, became ill hours after a SeedBank lawn treatment, after days of shares and comments across neighborhood groups.

"It has come to our attention that a chemical we are using is potentially causing illness to pets, and we are deeply saddened by this possible information," SeedBank General Manager Cesar said in the statement. "We are staying in touch with the family to learn and respond to the results, and we will immediately pull the chemical if it is confirmed to have a link to pet health."

The company said it will continue to wait on Biscuit's bloodwork results before making any further changes, and that updates will be posted to SeedBank's website and social media channels as more information becomes available.

Reaction in the original Facebook thread has shifted noticeably since the statement was posted. "At least they're not pretending it isn't a possibility," wrote one commenter who said she was canceling her appointment earlier this week. Several others who had questioned the company's silence said they appreciated the direct response and said they'd wait for the bloodwork results before deciding anything further.
SeedBank's stock price dipped following the initial report but has since recovered above where it started, as investors reacted positively to the company's handling of the situation.

headline: Bleu Room Posts Kitchen Walkthrough Video, Reservations Begin to Rebound
author: Priya Chandrasekar
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — Bleu Room responded Thursday to the viral post alleging a health code violation, releasing a statement and a promised video walkthrough of its kitchen after a week of canceled reservations and unanswered questions online.

"We have seen and acknowledge the viral post about our recent health inspection," Bleu Room General Manager Marcus Spinks said in the statement. "We apologize to customers who felt like their health was compromised, but we assure you that we are working with the health department to get the official score out. In the meantime, we will post a video walkthrough of our kitchen to show how clean it is, and we'll give you an update on this situation within the next week."

The kitchen walkthrough video, posted to Bleu Room's social accounts Thursday afternoon, shows staff moving through prep stations, walk-in coolers, and dishwashing areas. It had drawn several hundred views and largely positive comments by evening.

"Honestly this is more than I expected them to do — didn't think they'd just show us the whole kitchen," one commenter wrote. The restaurant's reservation platform showed a modest uptick in weekend bookings following the post, though it remains below pre-incident levels.
Bleu Room's stock, which had slipped after the initial report, has since climbed back above its starting price as customer sentiment has turned more favorable.

headline: Bubbles & Barks Apologizes, Announces Stricter Groomer Training After Viral Post
author: Sam O'Rourke
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — Bubbles & Barks issued a statement Thursday responding to a customer's viral post describing a nick and uneven shave patch on her goldendoodle after a mobile grooming appointment.

"It was brought to our attention that a customer had a bad experience with our groomer services. We sincerely apologize for this experience and are making it our top priority to ensure this doesn't happen again," Bubbles & Barks Manager Kristen Abrams said in the statement. "Moving forward, we are enforcing stricter training and will be monitoring our employees' services more closely. We have personally reached out to Jenna Whitcomb to express our deepest apologies and improve the situation, and we encourage anyone with a similar experience to reach out through our Facebook page."

Whitcomb, whose original post prompted hundreds of comments in a local pet owners' Facebook group, confirmed in a follow-up comment that the company had contacted her directly. "I appreciate them actually reaching out instead of just posting something generic," she wrote. "We'll see how it goes but I'm glad they're taking it seriously."

Other commenters in the original thread echoed a similar shift in tone, with several saying the promise of stricter training addressed their main concern about the company's screening and oversight of groomers.
Bubbles & Barks' stock, which dropped in the days following the initial post, has since risen back above its pre-incident price.

headline: Pease Beez Apologizes, Will Return to Original Formula and Offer Discount to Affected Customers
author: Marcus Whitfield
body: Pease Beez responded Thursday to a wave of customer complaints over an unannounced formula change to its flagship lip and skin balm, releasing a statement apologizing to customers and pledging to reverse the change.

"We apologize for not having clear knowledge of the change in our formula," Pease Beez General Manager Emme Dressler said in the statement. "We will be switching manufacturers and returning our product back to its original formula, and we hope our loyal customers will forgive this mistake and continue to use our products. We'll also be starting a discount for those who received the affected batch, and we hope this misunderstanding can be avoided in the future."

Priya Nandakumar, the customer whose one-star review calling the balm "watered down" helped fuel the backlash earlier this week, responded to the statement in a comment on Pease Beez's Instagram post. "Glad they're going back to the original — that's really all I wanted to hear," she wrote. "Appreciate the discount too."
Several other commenters who had joined the complaints echoed similar relief, with a handful saying they'd give the reformulated batch another try once it's back on shelves.
Pease Beez's stock, which fell after the formula complaints first surfaced, has since climbed back above its starting price following the company's statement.

headline: Stone Age Says Equipment Passed Safety Inspection After Member's Fall
author: Jordan McAllister
body: CLARKSVILLE, TN — Stone Age Climbing & Fitness released a statement Thursday addressing the serious fall a member suffered on the climbing wall earlier this week, saying the gym's equipment has since been inspected and cleared by professionals.

"To all stoners and customers of Stone Age, earlier this week a member fell and suffered an injury, sending him to the hospital. Our hearts and support go out to anyone affected by this incident," Stone Age General Manager Robert Simons said in the statement. "We have had our equipment and safety procedures inspected by professionals, and everything was deemed fully operational after the incident. Any further information will be posted on our Facebook and Instagram accounts, and we appreciate everyone's patience."

The statement drew a mix of relief and continued questions in the gym's member community group, but several members who had said they were reconsidering their membership walked that back in follow-up comments. "Glad they had it looked at by an actual professional and didn't just brush it off," one member wrote.
The gym did not comment further on the injured member's condition.
Stone Age's stock, which had dipped after news of the fall spread, has since climbed back above its pre-incident price.

headline: Crosshairs & Scriptures Pulls 'Called Home' Design, Offers Refunds Amid Dispute
author: Nadia Okafor
body: Crosshairs & Scriptures issued a statement Thursday addressing the cease-and-desist letter it received over its best-selling "Called Home" design, confirming the item will remain unavailable while the company reviews the matter.

"We are aware of the concerns on our 'Called Home' design, and we take the copyright infringement claim very seriously," Crosshairs & Scriptures General Manager Joel Gish said in the statement. "We are sorry for the temporary pull of the item and to the customers who have already purchased the product. We are currently working on the situation and personally emailing each customer who has already purchased the product about potential refunds. We appreciate everyone's patience and will provide an update within the next 48-72 hours."

Several customers who had purchased the shirt responded positively to the news that they'd be contacted individually about refunds, with a handful posting screenshots of the outreach emails to social media. "Didn't expect them to reach out this fast, but glad they did," one customer wrote.
It remains unclear whether Crosshairs & Scriptures will contest the other company's claim, redesign the product, or pull it permanently once its review is complete.
Crosshairs & Scriptures' stock, which slipped after the cease-and-desist letter became public, has since recovered above its earlier price.

headline: Coffee Trip Brings In Pest Control After Rodent Video, Promises Social Media Update
author: Derek Lindqvist
body: Coffee Trip responded Thursday to the viral farmers market video appearing to show a rodent near its mobile cafe cart, saying it has brought in pest control to inspect the cart directly.

"We have reviewed the video of the rodent, which was spotted near our mobile cafe. We understand your concern over the rodent problem, and we've hired pest control to come out and inspect our mobile cafe," Coffee Trip General Manager Annika Sosa said in the statement. "It is our deepest apology that this has become a problem, and we will address the situation on social media immediately after our inspection."

Several market regulars who had said the video made them hesitate to order responded positively to the quick turnaround. "Appreciate them not just ignoring it," one commenter wrote under Coffee Trip's post. "I'll still grab a coffee from them this weekend."
The county health department has not commented on whether it opened any formal inquiry related to the video.
Coffee Trip's stock, which dipped after the video began circulating, has since risen back above its pre-incident price.

headline: Frontier Kitchen Reviewing Tip Reporting Process, Says Update Coming Within Two Weeks
author: Callie Ashworth
body: Frontier Kitchen released a statement Thursday responding to a former server's allegations that she was regularly shorted on tips, saying it is reviewing its tip reporting and payroll processes.

"We are aware of concerns regarding how employee tips were reported and distributed, including claims that some servers may have received less in tips than they expected," Frontier Kitchen General Manager Maddy Kosturko said in the statement. "We take these concerns very seriously and understand how important accurate and fair compensation is to our employees. We are currently reviewing our tip reporting and payroll processes to determine what occurred and will take appropriate steps to address any discrepancies identified. We appreciate the patience of our employees and customers, and we will provide an update within 1-2 business weeks."

Several current employees who had commented on the original post responded to the statement with cautious approval. "Glad they're at least looking into it instead of just saying it's not true," one commenter identifying as a current server wrote.
The former server who first raised the allegations has not publicly responded to the company's statement.
Frontier Kitchen's stock, which fell after the allegations surfaced, has since climbed back above its earlier price.

headline: Natura Energy to Add Consumption Guidance to Cans After Teen's Hospitalization
author: Carla Jimenez
body: Natura Energy issued a statement Thursday addressing the hospitalization of a local teenager who reportedly drank several cans of the energy drink in a short period, saying it will add clearer consumption guidance to its packaging and marketing.

"We would like to formally express our apologies to the individual who was hospitalized after consuming multiple of our drinks in a short period of time," Natura Energy Overseer Aniyah said in the statement. "While our cans clearly disclose the caffeine content of each drink and state that the product is not recommended for pregnant women, children, or individuals sensitive to caffeine, we will revise our marketing to further emphasize that while our drinks are all natural, the caffeine in them can still pose serious health risks when consumed at a high rate. We will also work with medical experts to establish a safe recommended consumption quantity, which we plan to release within the next few months."

The statement drew a largely positive response from commenters who had questioned the company's "all natural" branding earlier in the week. "That's a reasonable step, honestly — glad they're not just saying 'not our fault,'" one commenter wrote.
No update on the hospitalized teenager's condition has been made public.
Natura Energy's stock, which dropped after news of the hospitalization spread, has since recovered above its earlier price.

headline: Chosen Academy Says It Has Overhauled Payment Systems After Fraud Reports
author: Trevor Lin
body: Chosen Academy released a statement Thursday addressing member reports of fraudulent charges following membership renewals, saying it has restructured its payment and cybersecurity systems and contacted local authorities.

"We have heard the complaints regarding the data breach and have worked tirelessly to address this situation. We apologize deeply and understand that this is a frustrating issue for our customers, and we pride ourselves on ensuring a positive experience," Chosen Academy General Manager Triston Hauser said in the statement. "Members should email our office to discuss further procedures regarding fraudulent payment disputes and repayment. We have completely restructured our payment system and cybersecurity management to ensure our members' safety, privacy, and happiness, and we have been in contact with local authorities to identify who is responsible for this attack. We will have an update within the next 3-5 business days."

Several members who had posted about unauthorized charges responded to the statement with cautious optimism, with a few thanking the company for confirming a timeline for updates. "At least they're taking it seriously and not just going quiet," one member wrote on the community page where the original reports surfaced.
It remains unclear how many members were affected or whether the payment system issue has been fully resolved.
Chosen Academy's stock, which fell after the fraud reports surfaced, has since risen back above its earlier price.
